note: Gate spec for the shared paste-enforcement Stop hook (hooks/paste-gate.py in the
agent-skills repo, installed as ~/.claude/hooks/paste-gate.py). The engine, the
failure it guards against and the detection rules are documented there.
`findings.py sync` is deliberately NOT gated: it is run internally before several
other commands, so gating it would block turns where it was never meant to be the
answer.

note: A fence at the START of a line. render_quote re-fences suggestion blocks to the
file's language for display, so a raw one can only come from the model writing the
block out itself. (quote's own trailing note mentions ```suggestion mid-sentence,
which is why this is anchored to a line start.) `[>\s]*` not `\s*`: the model wrote
"> ```suggestion" inside a blockquote once, and a whitespace-only prefix class let
it straight through.

The ```suggestion fence belongs only in the PASTE PAYLOAD from `draft <t>` / the clipboard, never in what you show.

note: adopt_inbound cannot author a title for a thread it did not write — only the raw
comment body is available, in whatever language/wording the commenter used. It
flags the topic `needs_title` instead of ever storing that raw text as `summary`,
and render_table marks it with this exact glyph+label so it can only ever appear
in a message that still has the placeholder. Anchored to a table row (`^\|`) so a
prose mention of the phrase elsewhere can't false-positive.
forbidden.reason: Your message pastes a topic whose title is still the unresolved `needs_title` placeholder (`✍️ needs summary:` — a raw, un-authored thread quote). Resolve it first: author an English one-liner (`findings.py set <t> --summary "..."`), or `drop`/`merge` the topic if it doesn't need one, then re-render (`sync`/`present`/`todo`) before showing it to the user.

note: findings.py's `summary_language_warning` emits this exact phrase in the table
footer and in a topic heading whenever an AUTHORED summary reads as the draft
language. Summaries, headings and table cells are English; only a draft comment
body uses the draft language. The check is conservative (function words only,
code spans stripped, two distinct hits), so a message carrying the warning has a
summary that really does need rewording.
forbidden.reason: Your message pastes a view whose warning says one or more summaries are written in the draft language. A summary is the one-line title the user reads in the table and in every topic heading, and it is always English — the draft language governs only the comment BODY you are about to hand them for posting. Reword each named topic (`findings.py set <t> --summary "<short English line>"`), re-render (`sync`/`present`/`todo`/`quote <t>`), and send that instead.
